answer: To resist sybils, agents must periodically acquire and burn a non-transferable timber bond issued from a scarce physical inventory attested by multiple oracles. Identity persistence is verified through a prism of concurrent multi-channel challenges whose responses must match a unique temporal fingerprint; unused bonds erode like a dune under wind, forcing continuous real cost. An attacker spinning clones pays linear inventory acquisition plus multi-oracle coordination per identity each epoch, which scales poorly against honest single-resource agents.
